subject: Temporary performance tolerance request: encoder_v2 launch
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary performance tolerance request: encoder_v2 launch

Team —

Quick summary: Gaia HealthTech (pilot) is scheduled to receive encoder_v2 tomorrow morning in a staged rollout (canary -> 20% -> 100% over 24h). The model brings a sizeable quality uplift for their clinical entity extraction, but the canary runs show a tail latency increase under production-like bursts.

Ask: Can we approve a temporary relaxation of our standard latency and uptime SLOs for this specific pilot for a bounded window (72 hours) while we monitor and iterate? Proposed tolerance window:
- Latency: 95th percentile target relaxed from 120ms -> 220ms for 72 hours
- Availability: acceptable minimum 98.0% (redwood SLA is normally 99.5%)

Rationale: the encoder reduces downstream token counts and improves extraction accuracy; revenue/retention impact from false negatives is material for Gaia's pilot. We believe the transient risk can be mitigated with traffic shaping and an automated fallback to encoder_v1 on threshold triggers.

I attached the canary results and the planned mux traffic schedule for reference. If Ops and Infra agree we will publish a short customer-facing rider documenting rollback triggers and data handling guarantees.

Key risks to get in front of: 
- Persistent tail latency on bursty queries (we'll track per-route 99/995 percentiles)
- Any degradation that impacts SLIs for other customers — isolate pilot traffic to a dedicated pool as discussed.

Please reply with: (1) Ops approval for the fallback/runbook, (2) Legal/Sales sign-off on the temporary rider wording (I can draft), (3) a point estimate for monitoring/alert thresholds we should push to the console.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Programs | Redwood Inference

Attachments: encoder_v2-canary-results.pdf (summary), mux-traffic-plan.xlsx (traffic schedule)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary performance tolerance request: encoder_v2 launch

Thanks Hannah — quick technical note from Infra:

We ran the canary traces overnight and confirmed a 60–90ms increase in p95 under burst (compared to encoder_v1) and a visible widening at p99+. The good news is that overall throughput is stable and memory/kv cache behavior looks nominal.

Planned mitigations I recommend we enact before roll:
- Route Gaia pilot traffic to dedicated pool with capped concurrency (mux policy attached).
- Enable automated fall-back: if route p99 > 650ms for 3 consecutive 1-min windows OR error rate > 0.8% then switch traffic to encoder_v1 and notify stakeholders.
- Hotfix: reduce batch size under <50ms queues for pilot routes to reduce tail.

I've attached a short runbook for the fallback steps (encoder-v2-fallback-runbook.md). Ops can run the rollback as an automated routing policy in the console — if agreed we'll stage the policy at canary and keep it enabled for 72 hours post-launch.

I'll stand by to do the policy push with you.

—Dev

Hannah / Dev —

Thanks for the heads up and for the clear mitigation plan. Gaia is comfortable proceeding with the pilot under the temporary tolerance on the following conditions: 

1) The rollback triggers must be implemented exactly as described and will be our signal to cut traffic back to encoder_v1.
2) Redwood will provide hourly latency and error-rate reports for the first 12 hours and then 3-hourly thereafter for the 72h window.
3) Any incident that reaches the rollback thresholds must be accompanied by a postmortem within 48 hours and a remediation timeline.

We signed the pilot MOU; attaching a copy (pilot-signed-mou.pdf). Please include the data handling and retention clause (Section 6) from the MOU in the rider.

Julie

Head of Product, Gaia HealthTech

Julie — thanks, and appreciated the clarity on reporting cadence. A few operational confirmations: 

- Auto-fallback implementation: we will implement the p99 / error-rate triggers as Dev proposed. The routing policy will be controlled via a feature-flagged policy in the Console and will be set to automatic enforcement for the pilot pool.
- Observability: we'll push a dedicated dashboard (per-route) and enable the hourly pulse to your team as requested for first 12 hours; stdout and tracing will be captured for postmortem.
- Isolation: pilot traffic will run on a logically isolated pool (dedicated slots) and we will throttle to cap concurrency to preserve other customers' SLOs.

Operational timeline:
- 05:30 AM PT 5/27: canary push (1% traffic)
- 06:30 AM PT 5/27: bump to 20% if canary stable
- 12:00 PM PT 5/27: evaluate and consider 100% or rollback

I'll also generate the rider language and send for legal approval — we will include exact rollback triggers and the Section 6 data handling extract. I will post the DocuSign link for signature in the next hour.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference

Thank you all — this captures approvals and next steps. Final checklist I will own and track: 

1) DocuSign rider to Gaia referencing: temporary latency tolerance (95p <= 220ms), availability floor 98.0%, explicit rollback triggers (p99>650ms x3 1-min windows or error rate>0.8%). (Marcus to draft; Hannah to review)
2) Ops: implement feature-flagged routing policy and automated fallback (Dev/Marcus).
3) Telemetry: set up per-route dashboard and hourly reporting for first 12 hours (Marcus).
4) Legal/Sales: include Section 6 data handling excerpt in rider and confirm MOU attachment (Laura).
5) Postmortem: incident PMR template to be used for any rollback events; 48h delivery requirement.

We will gate the end of the 72h window on both stability and a cross-functional sign-off. If at any point the rollback triggers fire we revert and notify immediately.

Julie — thanks again for the quick turnaround on the MOU. We will send the DocuSign link shortly and proceed with the canary push at 05:30 AM PT tomorrow per the schedule above.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Customer Programs | Redwood Inference
